sampling_model.design: Finite-period staggered adoption with a fixed, known canonical mapping from each implementation date to one complete announcement-and-implementation path, together with a fixed collection of not-yet-treated comparison risk sets.
sampling_model.units: Independent superpopulation draws of the complete observed panel vector; the number of periods and cohorts is fixed.
sampling_model.treatment: For cohort \(h\), the policy is announced or decided at known date \(\mathsf a(h)<h\), is not implemented before \(h\), and is first implemented at \(h\) and remains in force thereafter; outcomes may respond between \(\mathsf a(h)\) and \(h-1\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every cohort used by an observed graph edge or target has positive population probability; zero realized sample counts receive the full outcome-support band.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cohort--time means are estimated by sample averages and enclosed jointly by bounded-mean Hoeffding bands; endpoint computation optimizes over the entire simultaneous rectangle.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 identifies group--time average treatment effects using never-treated or not-yet-treated comparison groups under limited anticipation and the corresponding parallel-trends condition.
Section 4.2 derives staggered bounds using never-treated controls and observes that not-yet-treated comparisons require accounting for anticipation in the comparison group.
The paper derives anticipation bounds beginning with a classical two-period difference-in-differences model and gives a staggered extension focused on anticipation within treated cohorts.
The paper characterizes anticipation and timing-misclassification bias and constructs corrected estimators using groups known to be unaffected by misspecification.
The paper proves sharp partial-identification results by extending compatible lower-dimensional subdistributions to observationally equivalent full distributions.
Section 2 represents two-way fixed effects by an oriented incidence matrix and treats connected components through separate gauges.
The paper studies estimation and pointwise inference for sharp bounds that are values of generic linear programs, including multiple optima and failures of ordinary bootstrap regularity.
The paper derives asymptotic Gaussian-process simultaneous bands for an entire functional event-study path.

body.tldr: Announced staggered policies can make one future-treated cohort serve as an anticipatory comparison in several Callaway--Sant'Anna risk sets. Each implementation date is attached deterministically to one known complete path with a fixed earlier announcement date, no implementation before the cohort date, and absorbing implementation thereafter; the reference path has neither announcement nor implementation. Under a proposal-specific all-cohort additive mean restriction for the reference-path means and preregistered edgewise intervals for announcement-to-implementation responses, the reusable pre-implementation means form an edge vector whose admissible distortions are exactly an interval box intersected with the fundamental-cycle equations of the cohort--time graph. The project derives the fiber dimension on its minimal box face, proves that full box variation independence holds exactly when every positive-width edge is a bridge, characterizes nominal endpoint attainment by negative-cycle feasibility, and reduces every signed ATT aggregate endpoint to minimum-cost transshipment. The anchored zero-anticipation corner and a fully specified rational three-cohort contraction provide exact sanity reductions. Bounded potential outcomes are handled by an augmented interval-tension graph. The load-bearing open question is a regime-path-indexed completion theorem lifting every feasible mean vector to one common law of all path potential outcomes. Conditional on that completion, the affine region is causally sharp, and simultaneous Hoeffding bands yield a finite-sample honest outer confidence set by one joint optimization.

project_justification.gap: Callaway--Sant'Anna not-yet-treated comparisons reuse future-treated cohorts, but their point-identification result moves the base period outside a known anticipation horizon. Fenaroli's August 2026 Section 4.2 fixes never-treated controls and observes that not-yet-treated comparisons require accounting for anticipation in the comparison group. Existing bounded-anticipation work therefore supplies neither the joint compatibility restrictions across reused cohort--time means nor a full-law sharpness construction for that setting.
project_justification.niche: A deterministic, known canonical path for each implementation cohort makes the anticipated intervention well defined. The proposal-specific all-cohort additive mean restriction turns the no-announcement reference-path mean surface into an incidence-potential model, while separately calibrated edgewise intervals encode responses between the known announcement and implementation dates without importing Fenaroli's cohort-level increment bounds. Cycles rather than individual contrasts then determine compatibility, bridges determine variation independence, and arbitrary ATT weights become node demands in a transshipment problem.
project_justification.fill: The project gives a basis-invariant cycle theorem with a minimal-face affine-dimension formula, bridge and endpoint if-and-only-if frontiers, a bounded-outcome completion polyhedron, a min-cost-transshipment endpoint formula, and finite-sample outer coverage. Its anchored zero-anticipation formula and complete rational three-cohort instance make the normalization and contraction claims directly auditable. It isolates the only nonalgebraic step as an explicit full-law completion question over all canonical regime paths rather than assuming causal attainability.

body.related_work: CallawaySantAnna2021, Assumption 3 and Theorem 1, provides the not-yet-treated risk-set functional and the aggregation workflow consumed here; it removes anticipated cells through a known horizon rather than imposing the proposal-specific all-cohort additive mean restriction or bounding jointly reused contaminated cells. Fenaroli2026, Section 4.2, obtains cohortwise staggered bounds with never-treated controls and observes that using not-yet-treated comparisons requires accounting for anticipation in the comparison group. Its cohort-level increment bounds inform sensitivity calibration but are distinct from the edgewise path-response intervals imposed here, and Section 4.2 does not derive common cycle restrictions across reused comparison cells. Gong2022 builds anticipation bounds in a classical potential-outcomes DiD model and later considers staggered adoption, but its first changed proof step does not impose common cycle restrictions across overlapping comparison risk sets. AugustinGutknechtLiu2025 treats anticipation as timing misspecification, uses unaffected groups for correction, and documents the Indonesian anti-cheating application; magnitude-bounded contaminated comparison cohorts remain outside its correction strategy. PiccininniTchetgenStensrud2025 distinguishes interventions on policy decisions from interventions on implementation and motivates indexing potential outcomes by a fully specified deterministic path rather than by an implementation date alone. Torgovitsky2019 shows that a sharp low-dimensional characterization requires an observationally equivalent full-distribution extension, which is the completion obligation isolated here. Dawid2001 supplies the product-range definition of variation independence. JochmansWeidner2019 supplies the incidence, connectivity, and component-gauge language for two-way fixed effects. ChenKyngLiuPengProbstGutenbergSachdeva2022 formalizes minimum-cost flow through incidence balance, capacity, and cost constraints; the present work derives those objects from ATT weights and anticipation intervals. Voronin2025 analyzes generic stochastic LP values and active-face nonregularity, while the finite-sample theorem here avoids endpoint bootstrapping by propagating one simultaneous primitive-mean event. FangLiebl2026 constructs asymptotic simultaneous event-study bands; it does not cover a cycle-coupled identified region in finite samples.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exhaustive early kill test is computational evidence, not a proof. All 511 nonempty bipartite graphs with at most three cohorts and three periods were evaluated under randomly generated rational half-grid centers, positive and zero interval widths, disconnected components, feasible mean vectors, and deliberately perturbed mean vectors. Across 1,022 feasibility cases, the direct cycle-fiber linear program, node-potential interval-tension program, and negative-cycle certificate agreed. Across 299 feasible signed support cases, the direct fiber optimum, node-potential optimum, and split-flow transshipment dual agreed to numerical tolerance. No mismatch occurred. The test does not establish the announced-policy causal-completion property.
body.honest_scope: The cycle-fiber, minimal-face affine dimension, bridge frontier, endpoint certificate, transshipment dual, and finite-sample mean-band propagation are theorem targets. The dimension uses \(\mathcal I(\mu)\), not every positive-width primitive coordinate, whenever feasibility forces the fiber onto a proper box face. The zero-anticipation reduction is asserted only under the explicit rectangular risk-set anchor \(\mathsf{RA}\); without that anchor a target cohort gauge may remain unidentified. Theorems 4--6 are explicitly conditional on resolving Open-ended Question 1, and the predicate \(\mathsf{Comp}_3(z)\) records rather than assumes the worked instance's potential-outcome completion target. Bounded outcome support is enforced on every no-announcement reference-path cohort--time mean through the augmented complete bipartite tension graph, so the proposal does not infer a bounded full law from cycle equations alone. The mapping \(r\mapsto p^r\), every announcement date \(\mathsf a(r)\), and every edgewise sensitivity interval are fixed before outcome analysis. Within-cohort variation in announcement timing or content would require an observed path variable and a different model and is outside this proposal. Statistical learning of sensitivity magnitudes, covariate-conditional versions, continuous treatment timing, endogenous announcements, and uniform optimality of the outer confidence set are also outside scope.
